Coverage against the current website

This preview demonstrates the current design baseline. Geometry and component treatments can evolve together; the branding reference does not fix page layouts. The production specimens below share the website stylesheet. Static examples do not prove live provider behavior. The website currently includes a paginated technical blog, tag-filtered archive, consultation offer, dedicated contact page and English and Polish articles.

Specimens and remaining gaps
PatternCoverage
Brand, tokens and generic controlsDemonstrated below
Article bodyProse, highlighted code, TOC, downloads and article footer in the production specimen
Blog index and paginationArticle row and current/disabled pagination states in the production specimen
Archive filtering and searchInteractive search (results, empty, clear, Escape); static selected archive filter and empty state
Consultations and bookingRepresentative learning path, pricing, booking CTA and static provider fallback; actual form tested separately
Conference resourcesDownload and Polish Tally wrapper states in the production specimen; PDF viewing checked on the actual page
Icons and faviconsShared production SVGs and 16/32/180px identity assets; browser metadata and platform selection require production checks
ContactPrimary email action and secondary LinkedIn, X and GitHub links with decorative icons in the production specimen; shared CSS supports responsive inspection
About, Uses and 404Reading-layout excerpts and 404 recovery actions in the production specimen
Footer and cookiesShared footer, compact equal-choice panel, expanded disclosure; consent persistence tested on the website

See the design documentation review and the page-family requirements in DESIGN.md. Brand references supply the palette and updated logo; page composition is designed for the website.

07 / Content

Room for longer reading

Example article

The problem before the tool

Michał Mazur · 26 September 2026 · 4 min read

Changing a tool can be part of the solution. Start with the process and the decision that needs to be made. A short conversation can establish the scope.

Start with the problem and the constraints before choosing an implementation.

Before the conversation

  • A description of the problem and its effects.
  • An example from everyday work.

Working through the problem

  1. Define the expected outcome.
  2. Compare the available approaches.
  3. Test the selected approach.
Context
The conditions in which the problem occurs.
Constraint
A resource or requirement that affects the choice.
const problem = "Repetitive work";
const result = simplify(problem);
console.log(result);

09 / Website specimens

Production components

The scrollable preview shares the production CSS, local fonts and navigation/search scripts. Resize the browser to inspect mobile flow, including the Contact email and social links. Archive filters, provider states and consent are labeled static specimens; use the website regression suite for state persistence, history and provider loading.

CyberShu / style guide

Source: DESIGN.md · Inter license

Updating the preview

Generate tokens and specimens with pnpm style-guide:build. Use pnpm style-guide:watch to regenerate the file after source changes; refresh the browser to see the result. Freshness check: pnpm style-guide:check.

Source fingerprint: 1d156f07edf8. These specimens do not implement changes on the production website.
